question: Can orthogonality be derived as a necessary consequence of invariant-preserving non-redundant continuation?

results.claim: The ban on absolute identity alone does not uniquely determine orthogonality.
An invariant level-set gives a tangent continuation constraint.
With an independently established nondegenerate bilinear invariant q, local invariant preservation yields orthogonality to first order.
Non-redundancy alone yields independence from the existing span but not orthogonality.
Non-redundancy plus suitable symmetry/minimality plus bilinear invariant may select the orthogonal complement as canonical constraint.
If three realized external directions span a 3-dimensional carrier with nondegenerate q, the orthogonal complement is zero.

frontier.central_gap: Identify the invariant property that makes orthogonal continuation necessary rather than merely possible.
